A RESOLUTION OF TATTNALL COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS TO AUTHORIZE AND ENACT MORATORIUM RELATED TO LAND USE AND DEVELOPMENT INVOLVING CONSTRUCTION, PLACEMENT, MAINTENANCE AND IMPROVEMENTS OF DATA CENTERS; TO PROVIDE AN EFFECTIVE DATE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES ALLOWED BY LAW.

WHEREAS, as provided in the Georgia Constitution, the Tattnall County Board of Commissioners (“BOC”) enjoys home rule powers, including police power, and land development and governmental and supplementary powers, and the power to adopt such ordinances and regulations as necessary to perform all functions of government in order to promote and protect.the health, safety and general welfare of the citizens and general public of Tattnall County (“County”);

WHEREAS, the BOC finds that the ordered regulation of commercial and industrial development is necessary to protect the public health, safety, welfare and property values of the citizens of the County;

_ WHEREAS, the BOC from time to time reviews its ordinances to ensure that its laws preserve the quality of life for citizens while imposing limited and effective regulations on certain commercial and industrial development and uses that impact quality of life;

WHEREAS, the BOC intends to study the effects of data centers on the public health, safety and welfare of the County’s residents and businesses;

WHEREAS, the BOC intends to consider revisions to its Code of Ordinances (“Code”) designed to promote and protect the public health, safety and welfare of the County’s residents and businesses, including but not limited to access to power and water supply for the County's residents and businesses, through zoning classifications and/or regulations and standards for distance, noise and other ancillary impacts of data centers on surrounding properties,

WHEREAS, the BOC finds that it must take immediate and responsive action to protect the County, and it is in the best interests of the health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the County thatno applications be accepted in the unincorporated areas of the County for a period of 180 days from the effective date of this resolution if or where such applications relate to the establishment, construction, development and/or operation of data centers or those existing or under development, including any applications for special land use permits, rezonings, zonings, land disturbance permits, building permits, business licenses, or _certificates of occupancy;

WHEREAS, the BOC finds that itis in the County's best interests and that the aims and goals provided herein are best served by declaring and adopting a temporary

and limited moratorium to protect the public as a temporary measure to preserve ' the status quo;

WHEREAS, the BOC desires to strike an appropriate balance between the development of real property for data centers and any public concerns related thereto; and |

_ WHEREAS, in City of Roswell et al. v. Outdoor Systems, Inc., 274 Ga. 130 (2001), the Georgia Supreme Court held that limited. moratoria are reasonable and do not constitute land use when such moratoria are applied throughout the County; as well, the notice requirements of the Georgia Zoning Procedures Law do not apply to such moratoria;

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY DECLARED AND RESOLVED AS ~ FOLLOWS:

1, The moratorium imposed herein incorporates the findings and statements set forth in the preceding “WHEREAS” clauses and such clauses are made a part of this resolution. For the purposes of this resolution, “data center’ means a physical room, building, or facility that contains or houses infrastructure for building, running, operating, delivering or transmitting applications and services, or for storing and managing the data associated with those applications or services,

- 2. From the date of adoption of this resolution until 180 days from its adoption, notwithstanding any provision of the Code or County ordinance or regulation to the contrary, there shall be a complete moratorium on the acceptance of any applications relating to the establishment, construction, development and /or operation of new data centers or the expansion of currently existing or under development data centers, including any applications for special land use permits, rezonings, zonings, land disturbance permits, building permits, business licenses, or certificates of occupancy, in the unincorporated areas of the County and no licenses with respect to the establishment, expansion or development of the same shall be acted upon in the unincorporated areas of the County.

3, The BOC will study the effects of data centers on the health, safety and welfare of the County’s residents and businesses and report its findings

4, This moratorium will expire at 11:59 p.m. on the 180 day from the adoption of this resolution, unless shortened or extended by official action of the BOC.

- 5. The provisions of this resolution are severable and should any part of this resolution be deemed by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, such invalidity shall not affect the validity of the resolution as a while, or any part thereof other than the part declared to be invalid.
